title: What are the remaining angles of these two trapeziums?
description: In the first trapezium, each missing angle is one hundred eighty minus the angle across a slanting side. In the isosceles trapezium, the angles on one parallel side are equal and the other two are one hundred eighty minus them. The angles of each shape are added to check.
teaching_notes: One idea: between parallel sides, the two angles on the same side of a slanting side add up to one hundred eighty degrees. Watch for students who copy the parallelogram rule and give each angle the value of the angle opposite to it.

source: Figure it Out (kites and trapeziums, question 3)
video_script.why: The child finds the missing angles of two trapeziums by the method of the solved example: 180 minus the known angle, and equal base angles in the isosceles one.
video_script.substitution: the book's two trapeziums, one with angles of 105 and 135 degrees at the ends of a parallel side, and one isosceles trapezium with an angle of 100 degrees
video_script.anchor: the two trapeziums of the book with their angles marked
video_script.payoff_line: The remaining angles are seventy five and forty five, then one hundred, eighty and eighty

final_answer.spoken: for the first trapezium seventy five and forty five degrees, and for the second one hundred, eighty and eighty degrees

never_show: the two trapeziums given opposite angles that are equal
maths_rules: each slanting side cuts the parallel sides, so the two angles on its side add up to 180
in the isosceles trapezium the angles on one parallel side are equal, so the other one is 100
the two angles on the other parallel side are 180 - 100 = 80 each
video_script.design: One idea: 180 minus the known angle, and equal base angles in the isosceles one. The two trapeziums sit side by side and the angles are filled in one at a time.
open_questions: The book shows the angles in a figure only; which corner holds 100 degrees is taken from the worklist.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; two trapeziums side by side, the first with angles 105 and 135 degrees at the ends of one parallel side, the second an isosceles trapezium with an angle of 100 degrees

marks.one: the first trapezium appears with its two angles written
marks.two: the second trapezium appears with its equal slanting sides ticked
marks.ask: the missing angles glow with question marks

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about two trapeziums.
<bookmark mark='one'/>The first has angles of one hundred five and one hundred thirty five degrees.
They are at the ends of one parallel side.
<bookmark mark='two'/>The second is an isosceles trapezium with an angle of one hundred degrees.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Can you find the remaining angles?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the earlier trapezium and isosceles trapezium appear faintly with their angle rules

marks.sum: two angles on one side of a slanting side are joined to 180 degrees
marks.iso: the equal angles of an isosceles trapezium light up

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>We use the same method as the trapeziums in your book.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Two angles on one side of a slanting side add up to one hundred eighty degrees.
<bookmark mark='iso'/>In an isosceles trapezium, the angles on one parallel side are equal.

beats.on_screen: Given: (i) a trapezium with angles 105° and 135° at the ends of one parallel side; (ii) an isosceles trapezium with an angle of 100°
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a trapezium has angles of one hundred five and one hundred thirty five degrees.
They are at the ends of one parallel side.
<bookmark mark='iso'/>Also, an isosceles trapezium has an angle of one hundred degrees.

beats.on_screen: To find: the remaining angles of both trapeziums
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the remaining angles of both.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: (i) each slanting side cuts the parallel sides, so its two angles add up to 180°

marks.cut: the two slanting sides of the first trapezium light up in turn
marks.sum: each pair of angles is joined to one hundred eighty degrees

narration: <bookmark mark='cut'/>Step one, in the first trapezium, each slanting side cuts the two parallel sides.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>The two angles on its side add up to one hundred eighty degrees.

marks.a: one hundred eighty minus one hundred five is written at the first corner
marks.b: one hundred eighty minus one hundred thirty five is written at the second corner

narration: <bookmark mark='a'/>Step two, one hundred eighty minus one hundred five is seventy five degrees.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Likewise, one hundred eighty minus one hundred thirty five is forty five degrees.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: (ii) the slanting sides are equal, so the angles on the same parallel side are equal: the other one is 100°

marks.eq: the slanting sides of the second trapezium are ticked as equal
marks.pair: the two angles on the same parallel side light up
marks.val: one hundred degrees is written at the second corner

narration: <bookmark mark='eq'/>Step three, in the isosceles trapezium, the slanting sides are equal.
<bookmark mark='pair'/>The angles on the same parallel side are equal too.
<bookmark mark='val'/>The other angle on that side is also one hundred degrees.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: each angle on the other parallel side is 180 − 100 = 80°

marks.sub: one hundred eighty minus one hundred is written
marks.val: eighty degrees is written at each of the two lower corners

narration: <bookmark mark='sub'/>Step four, each angle on the other parallel side is one hundred eighty minus one hundred.
<bookmark mark='val'/>That is eighty degrees.

marks.chk: the four angles of each trapezium are added
marks.one: the first total three hundred sixty is written
marks.two: the second total three hundred sixty is written

narration: <bookmark mark='chk'/>Step five, the four angles of each trapezium should add up to three hundred sixty degrees.
<bookmark mark='one'/>One hundred five, one hundred thirty five, seventy five and forty five make three hundred sixty.
<bookmark mark='two'/>One hundred, one hundred, eighty and eighty make three hundred sixty as well.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The remaining angles are seventy five and forty five, then one hundred, eighty and eighty.
The first two belong to the first trapezium.
